item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-9a96a4fbd3b1a6f5","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"The government assigned 512,805 million pesos to 16 priority social programs in 2023, a real increase of 20 percentage points relative to the comparable 2019 program group; more than 40% of social-program spending went to these priorities. The largest increases included Fertilizers (+637%) and the older-adult pension (+123%), while emergency assistance fell 88% and health and medicines fell 35% relative to 2020.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly describes 2023 budgets and 2020-2023 changes under López Obrador; comparisons use different program universes for 2019 and 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the budgets and program choices to the current federal administration, but does not isolate López Obrador's personal decision from cabinet, legislative, or agency decisions.","limitations":["Budget allocation is evidence of priorities and resources, not by itself of service quality or causal outcomes.","The 2019 and 2023 program groups differ."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a96a4fbd3b1a6f5","start_unit":17,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL found that 13 of 16 priority programs adequately identified their target population in 2023, but three did not. Sembrando Vida used the ambiguous term 'subjects of rights' in its purpose despite more specific operating rules; Universities for Wellbeing, Reconstruction, and health/medicines had unclear or incomplete population and result definitions, with U013 reducing its purpose to a resource transfer.","question_ids":["5B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2023 monitoring evidence, with comparisons to earlier program designs where stated.","ruler_attribution":"The programs were federal priorities of López Obrador's administration, but the finding concerns program design and implementation rather than a personal act by the ruler.","limitations":["The document identifies design weaknesses but does not establish the reasons for each design choice or whether later corrections occurred.","It does not measure all program outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a96a4fbd3b1a6f5","start_unit":21,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"Older-adult protection received 52% of the 2023 priority-program budget through the pension program, whose purpose, target population, and indicators were assessed as appropriately specified. Health transfers received about 13% of the budget despite the health program lacking a clear target population; education received 8%, producers 13%, and the remainder covered children, disabled people, youth, and vulnerable populations.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 allocation and monitoring of federal priority programs.","ruler_attribution":"The allocation reflects federal administration priorities; the source does not attribute the decision solely to López Obrador personally.","limitations":["Budget shares do not establish equitable incidence or durable welfare effects.","The health-program classification indicates uncertainty about beneficiaries, not proof that funds were misused."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a96a4fbd3b1a6f5","start_unit":25,"end_unit":27,"fact_summary":"In 2023, 12 of 16 priority programs identified their thematic area fully or partially, but four were classified as Management because their central objectives did not identify a public problem clearly. These four programs represented almost 20% of priority-program funding and did not measure results; CONEVAL reports that recommendations and technical assistance were disregarded to varying degrees.","question_ids":["5B.7","6B.5","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Direct 2023 evidence, including the administration's response to monitoring recommendations over 2020-2023.","ruler_attribution":"The programs were administered by the federal government; the source does not identify which officials disregarded recommendations or whether López Obrador personally directed that conduct.","limitations":["'Disregarded to varying degrees' is not quantified program by program.","The finding concerns monitoring and design quality, not necessarily the absence of service delivery."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a96a4fbd3b1a6f5","start_unit":29,"end_unit":31,"fact_summary":"Only 14 of 16 priority programs had a valid coverage indicator for 2023. Using definitive 2022 data, 10 of those 14 exceeded their planned absolute coverage target, while four—disability pensions, guaranteed prices, urban improvement, and the wellbeing universities—fell short. Sembrando Vida and the health/medicines program had no coverage indicator.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.5","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report was issued for 2023 but coverage results are primarily definitive 2022 data, used as the latest available evidence for 2023 monitoring.","ruler_attribution":"The programs were federal administration programs; the evidence does not isolate presidential responsibility for coverage performance.","limitations":["Coverage is not equivalent to quality, uptake, welfare improvement, or equitable access.","Most quantitative coverage evidence predates the target year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a96a4fbd3b1a6f5","start_unit":33,"end_unit":39,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL found that 69% of priority programs had result-oriented purposes in 2023, but 19% had none and 12% needed improvement. Half measured results adequately, while four needed indicator adjustments and four did not measure results. Logical linkage between components and purposes existed in six programs, needed strengthening in eight, and was absent in two. Universities for Wellbeing worsened from 'needs improvement' in 2021 to 'no results orientation' in 2023; Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro improved its component design, while Producción para el Bienestar worsened in logical linkage.","question_ids":["5B.7","6B.5","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2023 assessment with 2021-2023 comparisons.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern federal program purposes and indicators under the administration, not a demonstrated personal decision by López Obrador.","limitations":["The assessment evaluates program logic and indicators, not the full range of actual outcomes.","Changes may reflect agency-level revisions, technical processes, or political direction; the source does not disaggregate causes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a96a4fbd3b1a6f5","start_unit":41,"end_unit":43,"fact_summary":"Between 2020 and 2022, the number of programs with adequate effective target compliance rose from five to nine, while the low-compliance category fell from five to one; deficient compliance remained at three. Several programs improved, including the older-adult pension, disability pension, youth employment, urban improvement, and reconstruction, while food-price guarantees, production support, and Universities for Wellbeing worsened or remained deficient. The older-adult pension achieved 1.00 for both results and management; Universities for Wellbeing achieved 0.213 for results and 0.482 for management.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.5","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report is a 2023 publication but the effective-target-compliance comparison covers 2020-2022.","ruler_attribution":"Performance is associated with federal programs of the administration, without proving personal presidential control over individual indicators.","limitations":["The metric is based on program indicators and target quality, not independent impact evaluation.","The latest compliance data are from 2022."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a96a4fbd3b1a6f5","start_unit":48,"end_unit":51,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL concluded that the administration's priority-program portfolio strongly funded older-adult protection and linked many programs to food, education, work, economic wellbeing, and social rights, but 19% of programs lacked clear target populations, 25% had ambiguous thematic purposes, 51% needed stronger component-purpose linkage, and two programs lacked coverage indicators. It identified clearer population definitions, better result logic, coverage measurement, and continued technical assistance as unresolved challenges.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.9","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Summary of 2023 monitoring, with some results based on 2022 data.","ruler_attribution":"The conclusions concern the federal administration's priority-program system; they do not establish López Obrador's personal role in each deficiency or correction.","limitations":["The document does not provide a counterfactual estimate of welfare effects.","Some conclusions aggregate heterogeneous programs and rely on prior-year data."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8cd79037d1d87b97","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The UN reported that Mexico's 2022 recovery included growth, foreign investment, job creation, and wage improvements, while programs for disadvantaged groups helped reduce poverty and income inequality; however, structural problems remained, including informality, inequality, insecurity, and incomplete recovery to pre-pandemic levels. The UN framework worked with federal, state, and local institutions and emphasized vulnerable populations and evidence-based planning.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","5B.1","5B.8","5B.10","6B.1","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report covers 2022, immediately preceding the target year, and describes conditions and institutional arrangements relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The UN describes cooperation with the Mexican State and government institutions, but reported results may reflect joint UN, federal, state, municipal, and civil-society action rather than López Obrador alone.","limitations":["The report is self-reported by the UN system and does not independently attribute national outcomes to the president.","It does not provide a complete 2023 outcome assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8cd79037d1d87b97","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"UN-supported programs helped enroll more than 54,000 domestic workers in social security, laid foundations for a National Care System, strengthened laws and services addressing violence against women, and supported reopening schools, teacher training, learning recovery, and dropout reintegration. The report also documents substantial remaining care, informality, education-loss, and rights gaps.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","4B.7","5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2022 implementation evidence relevant to the 2023 period; some results and institutional effects continued into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies collaboration with the Executive, legislature, IMSS, states, and civil society; attribution to López Obrador personally is not established.","limitations":["Reported achievements are joint-program results and may not represent nationwide coverage.","The report does not independently evaluate the durability or causal effect of each intervention."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8cd79037d1d87b97","start_unit":26,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"In 2022, cooperation with Mexican authorities strengthened laws and systems addressing gender violence, shelters, trafficking, missing persons, and human identification. The work included improved shelters, trained officials, support to victims, expanded staff for the Protection Mechanism for journalists and defenders, technically independent forensic identification capacity, and cooperation with families and search groups. These measures responded to severe violence, trafficking, and disappearance problems rather than eliminating them.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","6B.8","6B.9","8B.2","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2022 evidence relevant to the 2023 target period.","ruler_attribution":"The work involved federal and subnational agencies, UN bodies, civil society, and families; it cannot be attributed solely to López Obrador.","limitations":["The report records institutional activities and outputs, not a national reduction in violence or disappearances.","It does not assess whether all recommendations were implemented or violations remedied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8cd79037d1d87b97","start_unit":30,"end_unit":31,"fact_summary":"The UN reported that Mexico's government and partners developed a Sustainable Taxonomy, sustainable and gender-oriented bond financing, labor-market information systems, and partnerships across public, private, academic, and civil-society sectors. These instruments supported transparency, sustainable investment, labor reform monitoring, and climate or social objectives, while the report also noted dependence on international cooperation and the need for stronger coordination.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","7B.6","7B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly describes 2022 institutional and financing developments relevant to the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes these initiatives to joint work involving Mexican ministries, the legislature, UN agencies, private sector, and civil society, not solely to López Obrador.","limitations":["The report does not establish enforcement quality, fiscal sustainability, or long-term outcomes of the instruments.","Some financing and coordination were internationally supported."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8cd79037d1d87b97","start_unit":38,"end_unit":38,"fact_summary":"For 2023, the UN Country Team planned continued support for the National Care System, health-sector transformation, labor reform, energy transition, circular economy, school-dropout and learning recovery efforts, disability and Indigenous rights, migrant inclusion, climate agreements, anti-corruption, and journalist and human-rights-defender protection.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","4B.3","5B.6","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","7B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Explicitly concerns planned priorities for 2023, but describes intentions rather than completed results.","ruler_attribution":"These are UN Country Team priorities developed with federal counterparts; they do not demonstrate López Obrador's personal commitment or implementation.","limitations":["Plans are not evidence that the stated measures were enacted or effective.","No outcome data are provided for 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-240044c0f4fd6c00","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The World Bank assessed that López Obrador's administration prioritized universal transfers to older people, flagship public investment, the National Guard, the Isthmus corridor, Dos Bocas, energy self-sufficiency, labor reform, and macroeconomic stability. By 2023 GDP had grown 3.2% year-on-year, but potential growth remained subdued because of low productivity and investment; investment and regulatory uncertainty remained concerns.","question_ids":["3B.2","5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.10","6B.1","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers the administration and 2023 economic conditions, with comparisons to the pandemic period.","ruler_attribution":"The World Bank explicitly identifies López Obrador's administration and its priorities, though execution involved multiple institutions and external conditions.","limitations":["The source describes priorities and macroeconomic outcomes but does not establish that all outcomes were caused by presidential policy.","Growth was affected by the pandemic, U.S. recovery, nearshoring, inflation, and other external factors."]},{"source_id":"SRC-240044c0f4fd6c00","start_unit":9,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"World Bank implementation review found that only eight of 24 CPF objective indicators were achieved, one partially achieved, five on track, and ten off track; implementation was affected by the pandemic, policy shifts, institutional turnover, security obstacles, cancellations, and reduced demand for investment lending. The government requested restructuring or cancellation of multiple projects, while policy lending and analytical support continued.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.5","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The review was prepared in 2023 and evaluates the FY2020-2025 partnership at its midpoint.","ruler_attribution":"The review explicitly identifies client-requested cancellations, changing government priorities, and institutional capacity as factors, providing direct but not exclusive attribution to the administration.","limitations":["CPF indicators measure World Bank partnership performance, not the whole Mexican state.","The review combines outcomes from different years and projects and includes external shocks."]},{"source_id":"SRC-240044c0f4fd6c00","start_unit":16,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"World Bank indicators showed mixed economic and regulatory performance: 41 subnational laws or regulations introduced a pro-competitive framework, but the sustainable industrial-park framework had not been adopted by 2023; IFC nearshoring transactions remained at zero, and earlier grain-storage and market-information support was cancelled with targets missed. Digital payment use expanded to 17.9 million users and 8.7 million transactions by July 2023.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2023 indicator results, with some cancelled-project history from earlier years.","ruler_attribution":"The review attributes regulatory results and cancellations to World Bank-supported activities and government decisions, but not solely to the president.","limitations":["Indicators capture selected World Bank-supported interventions rather than the full economy.","The digital-payment indicator is an output measure and does not establish equitable access or welfare improvement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-240044c0f4fd6c00","start_unit":20,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"Education and social-service indicators were mixed: 31 states had adopted the early-childhood strategy by 2022, 6,390 schools had learning-recovery strategies by 2023, and IFC-supported health services exceeded their patient target. However, integrated state health networks were not implemented as planned because of policy changes and a new health model, while social-protection centers and employment-service modernization exceeded targets.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.4","6B.5","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly includes 2023 results and 2022 achievements under the administration.","ruler_attribution":"The World Bank attributes results to government and World Bank-supported systems; the failed health-network objective is linked to government policy change but not personally to López Obrador.","limitations":["Some patient figures come from IFC clients and are not national public-service outcomes.","Several indicators measure institutional adoption or outputs rather than sustained service quality."]},{"source_id":"SRC-240044c0f4fd6c00","start_unit":24,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"Climate and infrastructure results were mixed. World Bank-supported projects mobilized 1.95 billion dollars, generated 5,828 GWh, supported 45,168 households with housing, and expanded sustainable landscape management to 3.3 million hectares. Conversely, water-supply improvements were delayed, energy-efficiency savings were below the original target after project scaling-down, and some projects were cancelled or restructured.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2023 progress review with project histories spanning 2020-2023.","ruler_attribution":"Results reflect federal decisions, World Bank/IFC/MIGA interventions, and project implementation conditions; direct personal attribution is limited.","limitations":["Several figures are cumulative or projected and may not represent 2023-only effects.","Some outcomes are attributable to international-finance projects rather than government action alone."]},{"source_id":"SRC-240044c0f4fd6c00","start_unit":66,"end_unit":68,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported 3.2% GDP growth in 2023, 3.4 million net jobs created since March 2020, 2.8% seasonally adjusted unemployment in December 2023, and declining inflation. At the same time, the fiscal deficit was projected to reach 5.4% of GDP in 2024, debt increased, PEMEX remained financially weak, and the Bank warned that pension, social-program, and PEMEX spending could crowd out education and infrastructure.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2023 macroeconomic outcomes with 2024 fiscal projections used to identify inherited or emerging risks.","ruler_attribution":"The review links fiscal pressures to flagship investment, PEMEX support, pensions, and social programs of the administration, while recognizing external drivers such as nearshoring and U.S. demand.","limitations":["The 2024 deficit and debt figures are projections, not 2023 outcomes.","Macroeconomic outcomes have multiple domestic and external causes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-240044c0f4fd6c00","start_unit":70,"end_unit":75,"fact_summary":"During FY2020-2023, the World Bank recorded a sharp shift toward policy lending, ten project closures, four partial cancellations, four projects dropped during preparation, and two unsigned loan offers. It also recorded proactive restructurings, but noted that changing priorities, budget constraints, institutional turnover, procurement delays, and limited implementation capacity affected continuity and results.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.5","6B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers the FY2020-2023 implementation record relevant to the end of López Obrador's 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The review explicitly records government-requested cancellations and changing priorities, but also identifies World Bank and institutional factors.","limitations":["The record concerns the World Bank portfolio, not all federal projects.","Cancellation can reflect adaptation or failure; the document gives differing project-specific reasons."]},{"source_id":"SRC-240044c0f4fd6c00","start_unit":76,"end_unit":77,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that all active IBRD projects complied with citizen-engagement requirements and that gender tagging reached 100% of IBRD projects. It also reported climate co-benefits above corporate targets, while noting opportunities to deepen meaningful consultations with civil society and vulnerable groups beyond formal compliance.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.7","5B.7","6B.3","6B.8","7B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Portfolio evidence through FY2023, directly relevant to the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"These are World Bank portfolio practices and supported government projects; they do not prove López Obrador personally protected consultation or equality institutions.","limitations":["Compliance tagging and feedback indicators do not establish substantive influence or remedy.","The evidence covers World Bank projects rather than all government programs."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d058e2d993d39a07","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The IMF found Mexico's financial system resilient to severe macrofinancial shocks, with high bank capital and liquidity buffers and contained systemic liquidity risk. It nevertheless identified supervisory gaps involving autonomy and resources, consolidated supervision, cyber resilience, climate-risk disclosure, AML/CFT effectiveness, recovery and resolution planning, and the emergency-liquidity framework.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","5B.3","5B.7","5B.10","7B.6","7B.10","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment is based on information through July 2022, but its institutional findings and recommendations remained relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The IMF assesses Mexican authorities and financial institutions collectively; it does not attribute the framework or gaps personally to López Obrador.","limitations":["The report assesses the financial system, not the president's personal conduct.","Several findings are recommendations or risk warnings rather than observed 2023 failures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d058e2d993d39a07","start_unit":9,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"The IMF reported that Mexico had strengthened Basel implementation, supervisory techniques, cybersecurity capacity, recovery and resolution planning, TLAC requirements, and financial access measures. It also found unfinished work on regulator autonomy, consolidated supervision, macroprudential strategy, cyber oversight, climate disclosure, AML/CFT, liquidity management, and resolution tools.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","5B.3","5B.7","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Assessment published in 2022 and relevant to the institutional posture entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Findings concern Mexican financial authorities and regulatory institutions, not an isolated presidential decision.","limitations":["The report does not establish which reforms were enacted during 2023.","It evaluates technical financial governance rather than broad political integrity."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d058e2d993d39a07","start_unit":34,"end_unit":38,"fact_summary":"The IMF found that Mexico's financial authorities coordinated effectively during pandemic turmoil and had made significant progress in banking supervision and cybersecurity, but regulators lacked full budget autonomy and legal protection, agency resources had declined, several conglomerates were outside consolidated supervision, and cyber oversight and information-sharing required further strengthening.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.8","1B.9","1B.10","5B.3","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Evidence from the 2022 FSAP, relevant to 2023 institutional conditions.","ruler_attribution":"The IMF attributes the arrangements to Mexican authorities and legislation; personal presidential attribution is not established.","limitations":["The report records institutional design and recommendations, not a full assessment of López Obrador's appointments or directives.","Some findings reflect longstanding legal structures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d058e2d993d39a07","start_unit":39,"end_unit":43,"fact_summary":"The IMF found that Mexico's liquidity management was flexible and resilient during COVID-19 and that recovery and resolution plans existed for all commercial banks, but recommended stronger emergency liquidity rules, bail-in powers, resolvability, deposit-insurance funding, and development-bank liquidity oversight. Several 2016 recommendations remained unimplemented, including full supervisory and budgetary independence and consolidated supervision; system-wide crisis simulations had not been completed since 2011.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.8","1B.10","5B.3","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment covers conditions entering 2023; some unimplemented recommendations date from 2016.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern authorities and legal institutions collectively, not necessarily López Obrador's personal choices.","limitations":["The report is not a 2023 audit and does not show whether each recommendation was later implemented.","Financial crisis preparedness is only one dimension of national governance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d058e2d993d39a07","start_unit":44,"end_unit":46,"fact_summary":"The IMF reported moderate financial inclusion, limited competition, and persistent barriers for rural and small firms, while authorities supported a financial-inclusion agenda and claimed strong regulatory independence. It recommended wider fintech activities, faster open-finance implementation, more transparent development-bank use, and a national climate-finance strategy; the authorities agreed to consider the recommendations and publish the assessment.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10","8B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2022 assessment relevant to the 2023 policy environment.","ruler_attribution":"The report distinguishes IMF findings from authorities' views; neither establishes López Obrador's personal truthfulness or correction behavior.","limitations":["Authorities' stated intentions are not evidence of completed reforms.","Financial inclusion indicators do not directly measure distributional welfare."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents concern Mexico's federal programs, macroeconomy, social protection, World Bank portfolio, UN cooperation, and financial-system governance; they contain no material evidence about nuclear risk, international war or arms transfers, or most personal-integrity questions beyond institutional accountability and public-policy implementation.","Several sources cover 2022 or assessment periods ending before 2023; these facts are retained where they directly establish the institutional baseline, implementation trajectory, or 2023 monitoring context.","No scores or overall chapter judgments are provided."]}
